questions.q: What does "shared responsibility" mean for compliance in the cloud?
options: The customer is responsible for the physical data centers
Microsoft is responsible for everything, the customer has no compliance responsibilities at all
Microsoft is responsible for the compliance of the underlying platform; the customer is responsible for how they configure and use it
Compliance responsibility only applies to on-premises infrastructure, never to the cloud
questions.explain: Buying Azure provides a platform capable of meeting compliance requirements — it doesn't automatically make the customer's usage compliant.

questions.q: What is the Microsoft Trust Center?
options: Where Microsoft publishes Azure's compliance posture, certifications, and audit documentation
A management group used to organize subscriptions
The RBAC interface for assigning roles
A tool for estimating Azure costs before deployment
questions.explain: It's the real reference point compliance teams pull audit documentation from — not marketing material.

questions.q: Which framework specifically addresses EU regulation on personal data privacy?
options: HIPAA
GDPR
SOC 2
questions.explain: GDPR is the EU's data privacy and protection regulation; HIPAA addresses US health information instead.

questions.q: What level of compliance knowledge does AZ-900 (and this lesson) require?
options: Full mastery of every clause of GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, and ISO 27001
Only knowledge of US frameworks, since Azure is a US company's product
Recognizing framework names and knowing compliance is a real constraint — not mastering audit-level detail
No knowledge of compliance at all is expected
questions.explain: Deep compliance work is its own specialization; AZ-900 requires awareness, not mastery.

questions.q: Why doesn't "our data is on Azure" automatically make a company compliant with HIPAA or GDPR?
options: Because HIPAA and GDPR only apply to on-premises infrastructure
Because Azure has never met any compliance certifications
Because compliance also depends on how the customer configures and uses Azure — access, data placement, logging — which Microsoft doesn't control
Because compliance is entirely Microsoft's responsibility once data is on Azure
questions.explain: The platform being capable of compliance and the customer's actual usage being compliant are two different things — shared responsibility.
